extra.message: User input from request.GET['copyline'] is concatenated directly into an HTML string and returned with content_type='text/html'. No escaping is applied, allowing arbitrary HTML/JavaScript injection (reflected XSS).

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (Cross-site Scripting)

extra.message: User-supplied expression from request.GET['expr'] is passed directly to eval(). Although __builtins__ is restricted, class-based bypass techniques (e.g., ()__class__.__bases__[0].__subclasses__()) can achieve arbitrary code execution.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code (Code Injection)

extra.message: User-controlled 'lane' parameter from GET or POST is passed directly to Django's redirect() without validation. An attacker can craft a URL that redirects users to arbitrary external sites (phishing, malware delivery).

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site (Open Redirect)

extra.message: User-controlled 'fragment' parameter is concatenated directly into a Jinja2 template string. This enables Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI), which can lead to arbitrary code execution via Jinja2 sandbox escapes.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code (Code Injection)

extra.message: User-controlled 'name' query parameter is used directly in a file path without sanitization. An attacker can use '../' sequences to write arbitrary content (request body) to any location on the filesystem, potentially overwriting application files, configuration, or system files.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory (Path Traversal)

extra.message: User-controlled JSON body is deserialized and passed directly to MongoDB's find_one() as a filter query. An attacker can inject MongoDB operators ($ne, $regex, $where, $gt, etc.) to bypass authentication logic, extract data via boolean-based inference, or execute JavaScript with $where.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in NoSQL Queries

extra.message: patient_identity_ping_345 has no authentication gate (unlike all other ops endpoints). It does not call _wrk_gate() and accepts arbitrary unauthenticated requests. User-supplied 'handle' and 'channel' values are reflected in the response.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The DocumentForm accepts a file upload without any validation of file type, extension, or content. An attacker can upload arbitrary files (.html, .js, .exe, .py, etc.) which are stored on the server's filesystem under media/documents/. Combined with the DEBUG mode static serving, this could lead to arbitrary file execution or XSS.

cwe: CWE-434: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type

extra.message: The Authorization header (Bearer token) is logged in plaintext via logger.warning(). This exposes sensitive authentication credentials in log files, which may be readable by unauthorized personnel or included in error reports.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: Access-Control-Allow-Origin is set to the request's Origin header (or '*' as fallback) while Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is 'true'. This is a dangerously permissive CORS policy that allows any external site to make credentialed cross-origin requests, enabling CSRF-style attacks against authenticated users.

cwe: CWE-942: Overly Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: SSL certificate validation is explicitly disabled using ssl._create_unverified_context(). This makes the HTTPS request vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks, allowing an attacker to intercept or modify the response.

X-XSS-Protection is explicitly set to '0' (disabling browser XSS filters) and Content-Security-Policy is set to an empty string (removing all CSP restrictions). This removes critical browser-side security protections, making XSS and clickjacking attacks easier to exploit.

Staff role users (including clinicians and front desk) can filter messages by any patient_id via GET parameter without verifying they are assigned to or have a clinical relationship with that patient. This allows unauthorized access to patient communications.

Raw exception messages are displayed to users via messages.error(). This can leak internal implementation details such as database schema, table/column names, constraint violations, and stack traces, aiding attackers in reconnaissance.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: Hardcoded demo credentials (admin/adminpass, clinician1/clinicianpass, frontdesk1/frontdeskpass, patient1/patientpass) are defined in seed_data.py. If this seed data is run in production or the credentials are not changed, these well-known passwords can be used to gain unauthorized access.

random.choice() (Mersenne Twister) is used to generate a 'nonce' code. The random module is cryptographically insecure and predictable. An attacker who observes several outputs can predict future 'nonce' values.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG)

extra.message: Django is configured to serve static and media files directly via static() in DEBUG mode. The MEDIA_ROOT directory could contain sensitive documents. If DEBUG is accidentally left enabled in production, anyone can access uploaded files without authentication.
